sentences.text: There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
However in the light of the evidence of RW1 and 2, it is evident that the insured Auto was having permit to ply only at BBMP Geographical area.

That is to say he had plied the insured Auto outside the geographical area i.e., near Magadi.

sentences.text: On perusal of the above decisions the Honble High Court observed that plying the vehicle without permit and violation of the route permit are different.
The violation is complained is of route permit i.e. being territorial limits.
The same cannot be the defence for insurance company within the purview of sec.149(2) of M.V.Act.
Mere breach of permit condition, since such a defence plea is not a permissible under (2) of Section 149 of Act.
If the said vehicle found to have been ply in breach of permit condition it is open for concerned authority to take appropriate action.
But on that reason the insurance company cannot be absolved from liability.

Accordingly in the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.5960/2015 (MV-D) C/w  23  SCCH-23  MVC.6354/2023 C/w MVC.6355/2023 MFA.No.706/2013 (MV-D) and MFA.No.102428/2017 also Hon'ble High Court has taken same observation.
In the present case also the Auto was having permit for plying in the BBMP limits only but the driver of the Auto was taken over the vehicle outside of the permit area.
Only on that reason it cannot be held that the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation.
It is not violation of conditions of insurance.

The violation is complained is of route permit i.e. being territorial limits.
The same cannot be the defence for insurance company within the purview of sec.149(2) of M.V.Act.
Mere breach of permit condition, since such a defence plea is not a permissible under (2) of Section 149 of Act.
